source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Abdulbari,

Somewhere my intended message got lost in translation. I know it’s hard to read my mind when I use more abstract terms, and I think I was trying to ask you to change too many things at once, which is why we have taken a couple of steps in the wrong direction.

I’m attaching this image for reference because it was the closest rendering to what I wanted to refine. Instead of changing the length and exploring the terminations at the same time, we’re going to focus strictly on height.

Could you please show the following as a calibrated progression in both the Hero V and the second V? The second V should remain proportionally scaled to its own size, so each increase should be calculated relative to the total height of that individual V.

Original Option B as the control
Original Option B with the right endpoint approximately 1% higher
The same treatment at approximately 2% higher
The same treatment at approximately 3% higher

Please keep the existing slope, terminal shape, taper, and all other geometry exactly as shown in the original Option B. Only the height of the right endpoint should change. Once the correct percentage is established, the É accent should follow that same proportional relationship.

I know this is an exceptionally small distinction, but I believe the relationship between the left and right endpoints will become one of the defining details shared across the Hero V, second V, and É accent. I want it to be almost imperceptible, but still enough to distinguish it from a more average V.

Thank you for helping me isolate it with this level of precision.

value_updates.terminal_status: reopened only for the calibrated right-endpoint height study
value_updates.experimental_control: Original Option B with its existing slope, terminal shape, taper, and all other geometry unchanged while only right-endpoint height is varied
value_updates.consistency_rule: Calibrate the Hero V and second V relative to each glyph's own total height, then apply the selected proportional relationship to the É accent

decisions.reason: The source isolates endpoint-height changes to the V-system signature elements and explicitly keeps all other geometry unchanged; it does not modify the E or L letterform requirements.
The proportional endpoint-height study does not change the established hierarchy: the second V remains subordinate to the Hero V, with only its right arm extending subtly above the alphabet.
Requiring the É accent to follow the selected Hero V proportional relationship preserves rather than changes the existing exact peak-alignment requirement.
The source changes only endpoint height and does not alter the selected Satin Reflection finish, champagne-gold distribution, or other material-treatment attributes.
The source isolates endpoint height while keeping spacing and all other established geometry locked, so the Balanced Flow kerning remains unchanged.
The endpoint-height progression does not change the established E/L cap-height alignment to the second V's left arm.
The source provides design feedback for a height study but does not change the standing obligation to explain the intent of review rounds.
Changing only the right endpoints' height does not alter the common baseline alignment of the V bottom points with the E and L.
